record.original_question: Assume F is a foliation of geometric degree d ≥ 2 on P2, the line at infinity is invariant, and all singularities are hyperbolic. Do all non-compact leaves of F, meaning all leaves except the compact curves, admit Green functions?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1. (i) Assume that F is a foliation of geometric degree d ≥ 2 on P2 with the line at infinity invariant and having only hyperbolic singularities. Do the leaves, except for the compact curves, have Green functions ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a singular holomorphic foliation by curves on the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$ of geometric degree $d \geq 2$ (the geometric degree being the number of tangencies of $\mathcal{F}$ with a generic projective line). Assume that:

(i) the line at infinity $L_\infty \subset \mathbb{P}^2$ is invariant under $\mathcal{F}$, and

(ii) every singular point of $\mathcal{F}$ is hyperbolic, i.e., at each singular point the linear part of a local vector field defining $\mathcal{F}$ has two nonzero eigenvalues whose ratio is not a positive real number.

A leaf $L$ of $\mathcal{F}$ (viewed as a Riemann surface via its immersion into $\mathbb{P}^2$) is said to admit a Green function if it is hyperbolic in the sense of potential theory, that is, if it carries a non-constant negative subharmonic function (equivalently, if its universal cover is the unit disk and it admits a classical Green function with logarithmic pole).

Question: Under the above hypotheses, does every non-compact leaf of $\mathcal{F}$ (i.e., every leaf other than those supported on a compact algebraic curve) admit a Green function?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about the existence of Green functions on leaves of degree-$d \geq 2$ foliations of $\mathbb{P}^2$ with invariant line at infinity and only hyperbolic singularities. Searches turned up related results on hyperbolicity of leaves and absence of directed positive closed currents under similar hypotheses, but no source resolving this specific question in either direction. It appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Topology and Complex Structures of Leaves of Foliations by Riemann Surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies leaves of foliations by Riemann surfaces with hyperbolic singularities; discusses when generic leaves are hyperbolic and carry Green functions, but does not resolve the stated question for all non-compact leaves on P^2.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on hyperbolicity of leaves but no full resolution.

status_evidence.title: Uniformization and the Poincaré metric on the leaves of a foliation by curves
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses uniformization of leaves of singular holomorphic foliations and the Poincaré metric, foundational for the notion of Green functions on leaves.
status_evidence.claim: Background framework but does not answer the specific problem.
